title: Clinical comparison finds automated and manual vena-cava indices are not interchangeable during assisted ventilation
summary: In 23 intensive-care patients receiving pressure-support ventilation, the learned Auto IVC tool and conventional M-mode produced distensibility-index measurements with wide agreement limits. Measurements from different imaging windows also lacked adequate agreement. This is a small clinical measurement-validation study; it does not establish fluid responsiveness, patient benefit or that either method gives the true physiological value.
ai_technology: GE Venue Go R2 Auto IVC learned ultrasound localization and automated measurement
organization: Medical University of Warsaw; University of Catania

evidence.tested: Single-center prospective paired measurement comparison in 23 intubated patients on pressure-support ventilation. The same operator acquired M-mode and Auto IVC measurements in subcostal and trans-hepatic views; the latter view was unavailable in four patients. Offline manual measurement was blinded to automated results. Automated-minus-manual distensibility-index mean biases were about six percentage points, with broad Bland–Altman limits rather than interchangeable measurements.
evidence.unknown: One operator and center, small cohort, fixed acquisition order and repeated automated measurements limit generalization. Manual M-mode is a comparator rather than a definitive physiological reference. The source did not test treatment decisions, fluid responsiveness or clinical outcomes. The proprietary model architecture and training cohort are not independently audited.
evidence.ai_role: The study Methods identify Auto IVC on Venue Go R2 as the measurement tool; original vendor documentation describes training on thousands of ultrasound images to locate the vessel and place/track the measurement cursor before calculating respiratory diameter indices. Those learned measurements are directly evaluated in the paired clinical comparison.

source_review.scope: Read actual original cohort, named device/tool, paired acquisition/blinding, repeated-measurement agreement Methods, clinical Results and limitations; original vendor trained-algorithm description corroborates the learned enabling operation. Original publication May31 distinguished from later issue. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
